blocks.text: DSPM leverages Jira APIs to automatically create tickets when sensitive data or any misconfigurations are detected in your cloud resources. You can integrate DSPM with Jira to leverage the alert data logs from the cloud storage services and create incidents for further evaluation.
DSPM can be integrated with Jira cloud versions, provided there is support for the required authentication mechanism and APIs to create a Jira task.
You must first complete the OAuth configuration before integrating DSPM with Jira.

blocks.item: 1. Configure the OAuth app.
Sign in to the Atlassian Developer console.
Click Create and select OAuth 2.0 integration.
See image.
Under Create a New OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration, enter a name for the application.
See image.
Accept the terms and conditions, then click Create.
The application is created and displayed under Console > My apps.
2. Set up the API permissions.
On the Atlassian Developer console, click Permissions.
Click Add for the Jira API.
See image.
The button name changes to Configuration.
Click Configuration to view the list of Jira APIs.
Select the scope for the required Jira features that you want to use for this integration. For example, select read:jira-work to read the Jira project, issue data, etc.
See image.
Click Save.
3. Authorize DSPM to access the Jira APIs.
Go to the Zscaler Admin Console and copy the application URL.
See image.
On the Atlassian Developer console, click Authorization in the left-side navigation.
Click Add.
For Callback URL, paste the application URL you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
Click Save Changes.
Next, click Settings in the left-side navigation.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. You need to use these values while adding the Jira integration in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > DSPM Integrations.
Click Add next to the ITSM integration.
See image.
The Add ITSM Integration page appears.
On the Add ITSM Integration page, under Integration Details:
Integration Name: Enter a unique name for the integration.
IT Service: Select Jira.
See image.
Click Next.
Under ITSM Details, complete the following steps to authorize DSPM to create tickets in Jira:
Client ID: Paste the Client ID that you copied while configuring the OAuth app.
Client Secret: Paste the Client Secret that you copied while configuring the OAuth app.
Authorize: Click to validate the connection between DSPM and the Jira account.
See image.

You are redirected back to the Atlassian login page. If you're not able to log in, then you see the Authorization in Process message in the Zscaler Admin Console, and the following message on the Atlassian Developer console: See image. Check and use the correct Client ID and Client Secret values for the authorization to be successful.
On the Atlassian Developer console, click Accept to grant the required permissions to the OAuth client app to perform API operations in Jira.
See image.
You are again redirected back to the Zscaler Admin Console and a message is displayed indicating the authorization is successful.
Select the required Jira project from the drop-down menu.
Click Next.
Review the integration details. Click the Edit icon if you want to make any changes.
See image.
Click Finish.

blocks.text: The integration is added, and the details are displayed on the Integrations page. To complete the integration process and enable data transmission, you must configure and associate the alert notification rules with this integration for DSPM to be able to send the data logs.
